structure.overview: The case concerns the judicial review of a visa officer's refusal to process a post-graduate work permit application submitted by a Brazilian citizen who was outside Canada due to COVID-19 travel restrictions. The applicant challenged the refusal on the basis that the application should have been processed as an out-of-Canada application. The Federal Court found the refusal unreasonable, set aside the decision, and remitted the matter for redetermination with directions to treat the application as out-of-Canada.

sections.label: Standard of review and analysis of decision

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The applicant seeks judicial review of a visa officer's January 25, 2022 decision refusing a post-graduate work permit application; the court will allow the review.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The applicant, a Brazilian citizen, was completing her degree in Edmonton but had to return to Brazil in March 2020 due to a family emergency and COVID-19 travel restrictions prevented her return.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Despite being stuck in Brazil, the applicant completed her degree on time as MacEwan University suspended classes and moved exams online due to the pandemic.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: In May 2020, while in Brazil, the applicant applied online for a post-graduate work permit, believing she was still legally resident in Canada and submitted form IMM 5710 with an explanatory letter.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: On November 17, 2021, IRCC refused the application because the applicant was outside Canada and thus ineligible to apply to change conditions or extend stay from within Canada.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The applicant retained counsel who submitted a detailed reconsideration request on December 9, 2021, challenging the refusal.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Counsel argued the applicant used the wrong form initially, submitted the correct form later, met eligibility requirements, and requested reconsideration due to IRCC's delay causing a missed application timeframe.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Counsel noted the applicant's eligibility for the work permit did not depend on whether she was inside or outside Canada when applying.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Counsel requested that if the visa officer could not process an out-of-Canada application, the application be forwarded to the appropriate IRCC decision maker.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: On January 25, 2022, the IRCC officer confirmed the refusal, stating the application could not be processed as an out-of-Canada application and a new application was required.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The parties and court agree the officer's decision should be reviewed on a reasonableness standard.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains the reasonableness standard requires decisions to be coherent, rational, justified, intelligible, and transparent per Vavilov.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds the officer's refusal to treat the application as out-of-Canada unreasonable, noting no legal basis for the refusal and that a new application would fail due to timing.
idea_list: new application would fail due to timing

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The officer's decision is set aside and the matter is remitted for redetermination.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court directs IRCC to treat the application as out-of-Canada, use the original lock-in date, request additional info within 30 days, allow applicant to update info, and decide expeditiously.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court agrees with parties that no serious questions of general importance arise for certification under IRPA section 74(d).
